Maintenance Report — MNT-0096-003

Asset: WELL-0096 (SW-24 Well 096, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 05 Mar 2023 08:00 · Finished: 07 Mar 2023 23:00 · Well stopped for this job: 63 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0096-0020 on 2023-03-02 Report written: 07 Mar 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0096-0020 showed the wellhead at 12.9 °C with the air at 11.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale.

Root cause

Sand and scale build-up in the pump barrel.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0096-009

Asset: WELL-0096 (SW-24 Well 096, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 17 Nov 2023 08:00 · Finished: 18 Nov 2023 02:00 · Well stopped for this job: 18 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0096-0056 on 2023-11-16 Report written: 18 Nov 2023

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0096-0056 at 10:30 on 2023-11-16 found crude oil on the pad: about 10.9% of the pad area, estimated 4.2 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.4 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).

  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 261 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 209 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.8 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0096-009 (WS-06).

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0096-0063 showed the wellhead at 6.2 °C with the air at 5.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. Maintenance Report — MNT-0096-028

Asset: WELL-0096 (SW-24 Well 096, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: rod string Work started: 27 Sep 2025 08:00 · Finished: 30 Sep 2025 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 72 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0096-0152 on 2025-09-25 Report written: 30 Sep 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running but the wellhead was cold and the rod load had dropped. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0096-0152 showed the wellhead at 25.8 °C with the air at 23.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod.

Root cause

A coupling unscrewed after repeated rod buckling at the bottom of the stroke.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

maintenance.action: Replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0096-034

Asset: WELL-0096 (SW-24 Well 096, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 15 May 2026 08:00 · Finished: 16 May 2026 14:00 · Well stopped for this job: 30 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0096-0184 on 2026-05-14 Report written: 16 May 2026

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0096-0184 at 12:00 on 2026-05-14 found crude oil on the pad: about 6.2% of the pad area, estimated 2.8 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.7 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 261 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 209 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.2 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0096-034 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.86% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).
